answerBody: S. 5653, the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, pairs two different data-center cost rules inside one section. One would direct FERC to revise its 1994 transmission pricing policy so computational loads pay both embedded grid costs and incremental transmission costs, with no megawatt cutoff. The other, a proposed Federal Power Act floor, would bar shifting incremental generation, storage, transmission, and distribution costs of covered computing loads of 20 megawatts or more onto other customers, and would require financial assurances. Congress must now choose the governing cost rule for data-center grid charges before the new Congress convenes: enact the size-neutral transmission pricing rewrite, or enact the 20-megawatt incremental-cost floor. Which rule should govern?
rationale: Delta: Genesis asked pass-the-package versus a narrower rewrite. The selected Spring answered hold, treating the 20 MW floor, assurances, and early-exit recovery as the separable piece worth keeping. This fork rejects that premise by splitting the cost title itself. Section 2107 pairs a size-neutral FERC rewrite of the 1994 higher-of policy—computational loads pay embedded and incremental transmission costs—with a 20 MW FPA floor covering generation, storage, transmission, and distribution. Those rules differ in threshold, cost base, and jurisdiction. History is empty, so this is not a replay or option reversal. Either rule can be defended: “and” pricing targets the estimated transmission shift without a retail generation mandate; the 20 MW floor matches state but-for practice and stranded-cost risk but leaves sub-20 MW and embedded costs open. A compromise of both restates the Spring and does not answer which rule governs.
